1→# Coding Conventions
     2→
     3→**Analysis Date:** 2026-02-02
     4→
     5→## Naming Patterns
     6→
     7→**Files:**
     8→- C++ source files: `snake_case.cpp` (e.g., `my_final.cpp`, `my_canvas.cpp`, `matrix_transform.cpp`)
     9→- C++ header files: `snake_case.h` or `PascalCase.h` in include directory
    10→  - Public headers in `include/`: `PascalCase.h` (e.g., `GCanvas.h`, `GMatrix.h`, `GPaint.h`)
    11→  - Implementation headers in root: `snake_case.h` (e.g., `my_utils.h`, `blend_functions.h`, `shader_ops.h`, `path_ops.h`, `Edge.h`)
    12→- HTML files: `snake_case.html` (e.g., `graphics-demo.html`, `admin.html`)
    13→
    14→**Functions:**
    15→- C++ member functions: `camelCase` (e.g., `drawShape()`, `shadeRow()`, `isOpaque()`, `setContext()`)
    16→- C++ class methods: `camelCase` (e.g., `unpremult()`, `pt_coons_avg()`)
    17→- JavaScript functions: `camelCase` (e.g., `hexToRgba()`, `drawShape()`, `clearCanvas()`, `toggleAnimation()`)
    18→- Utility functions: `snake_case` (e.g., `pt_coons_avg()`, `pt_weighted_avg()`)
    19→
    20→**Variables:**
    21→- C++ member variables: `fPrefixedCamelCase` (e.g., `fColor`, `fShader`, `fMode`, `fDeps`, `fSrc`)
    22→- C++ local variables: `camelCase` (e.g., `x`, `y`, `color`, `rotation`, `scale`, `propC1`)
    23→- JavaScript constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` (e.g., `PASSWORD_HASH`)
    24→- JavaScript variables: `camelCase` (e.g., `canvas`, `ctx`, `shapeType`, `colorPicker`)
    25→
    26→**Types:**
    27→- C++ classes: `PascalCase` (e.g., `LinearPosGradientShader`, `MyFinal`, `GCanvas`, `GPaint`, `GMatrix`)
    28→- CSS classes: `kebab-case` (e.g., `.project-grid`, `.project-card`, `.skill-badge`, `.control-group`)
    29→- CSS ID selectors: `camelCase` (e.g., `#canvas`, `#shapeType`, `#colorPicker`, `#loginContainer`)
    30→
    31→## Code Style
    32→
    33→**Formatting:**
    34→- No explicit formatter configured
    35→- CSS inline styles: Properties use standard CSS with hyphenated names
    36→- JavaScript: 4-space indentation observed in closures and control structures
    37→- HTML: 4-space indentation for nested elements
    38→- C++: Uses standard C++17 compilation with `-Wno-narrowing`, `-Wreturn-type`, `-Wunused-function`, `-Wreorder` warnings enabled
    39→
    40→**Linting:**
    41→- C++ compilation flags: `-g -Wno-narrowing -Wreturn-type -Wunused-function -Wreorder -Wunused-variable -Wfloat-conversion`
    42→- Standard: C++17 (`-std=c++17`)
    43→- Release builds: Include `-O3 -DNDEBUG` optimization flags
    44→- No explicit linter configuration detected (no `.eslintrc`, `.prettierrc`, etc.)
    45→
    46→## Import Organization
    47→
    48→**C++ includes:**
    49→Order follows include guard pattern with three categories:
    50→
    51→1. **Standard library**: `#include <string>`, `#include <vector>`, etc.
    52→2. **Project headers**: `#include "include/GCanvas.h"`, `#include "include/GMatrix.h"`, etc.
    53→3. **Commented-out legacy includes**: Older headers marked with `//` prefix
    54→
    55→Example from `my_final.cpp`:
    56→```cpp
    57→#include "include/GBitmap.h"
    58→#include "include/GCanvas.h"
    59→#include "include/GColor.h"
    60→// ... more public headers ...
    61→#include "include/GFinal.h"
    62→// #include "starter_canvas.h"  (legacy, commented out)
    63→// #include "Edge.h"
    64→```
    65→
    66→**JavaScript imports:**
    67→- Uses global scope variables accessed via `document.getElementById()`
    68→- No module system (inline `<script>` tags)
    69→- Variables declared with `const` for constants and DOM elements
    70→
    71→## Error Handling
    72→
    73→**Patterns:**
    74→- C++ assertions used for validation: `assert(prop <= positions[k]);`, `assert(propC1 >= 0.0f && propC1 <= 1.0f);`
    75→- HTML form validation via `required` attribute on input fields
    76→- JavaScript error display via CSS class toggling: `error.classList.add('show')` and `error.classList.remove('show')`
    77→- User feedback through input state clearing: `document.getElementById('password').value = ''`
    78→
    79→## Logging
    80→
    81→**Framework:** `console` object (not observed in codebase)
    82→
    83→**Patterns:**
    84→- No explicit logging statements found in codebase
    85→- No structured logging framework detected
    86→- Console operations not used in graphics engine or web UI
    87→
    88→## Comments
    89→
    90→**When to Comment:**
    91→- File-level copyright headers: Observed in public header files (e.g., `GCanvas.h`)
    92→- Algorithm documentation: Detailed JSDoc-style comments in header files explaining parameter usage and behavior
    93→- Legacy code markers: Commented-out includes indicate deprecated functionality
    94→- Type documentation: Comments explain complex type parameters
    95→
    96→**JSDoc/TSDoc:**
    97→- C++ style: Multi-line comments with detailed explanations
    98→- Example from `GCanvas.h`:
    99→```cpp
   100→/**
   101→ *  Save off a copy of the canvas state (CTM), to be later used if the balancing call to
   102→ *  restore() is made. Calls to save/restore can be nested:
   103→ *  ...detailed example...
   104→ */
   105→virtual void save() = 0;
   106→```
   107→- JavaScript: Sparse, minimal comments except for critical business logic (e.g., password hashing algorithm)
   108→- HTML: Minimal comments except for demarcating major sections (`<!-- Login Form -->`, `<!-- Code Viewer -->`)
   109→
   110→## Function Design
   111→
   112→**Size:**
   113→- C++ shader functions: Medium (60-110 lines for complex algorithms like `shadeRow()`)
   114→- JavaScript functions: Small to medium (10-50 lines)
   115→- HTML event handlers: Small inline closures
   116→
   117→**Parameters:**
   118→- C++ uses const references for arrays and objects: `const GColor colors[]`, `const GMatrix& ctm`
   119→- C++ member functions commonly use `this` returns for chaining: `GPaint& setColor(GColor c) { fColor = c; return *this; }`
   120→- JavaScript closures capture variables from outer scope
   121→
   122→**Return Values:**
   123→- C++ bool returns for status: `bool setContext(const GMatrix& ctm) override`
   124→- C++ optional pattern: `if (auto inverse = m.invert()) { ... }`
   125→- C++ void for drawing operations
   126→- JavaScript direct value returns for utility functions
   127→
   128→## Module Design
   129→
   130→**Exports:**
   131→- C++ class definitions in `.h` files define the public interface
   132→- All implementation in `.cpp` files
   133→- Header-only utility headers for template-like code: `my_utils.h`, `blend_functions.h`
   134→
   135→**Barrel Files:**
   136→- Not used in C++ codebase
   137→- HTML pages are standalone (index.html, graphics-demo.html, admin.html)
   138→- No aggregated exports observed
   139→
   140→## C++ Specific Conventions
   141→
   142→**Class Hierarchy:**
   143→- Inheritance indicated by `: public BaseClass` syntax
   144→- Virtual method overriding with `override` keyword: `bool setContext(const GMatrix& ctm) override`
   145→- Pure virtual base classes used for interfaces (e.g., `GCanvas`, `GShader`, `GFinal`)
   146→
   147→**Constructor Patterns:**
   148→- Initializer lists used: `LinearPosGradientShader(...) : P0(p0), P1(p1), count(count)`
   149→- Default member initialization: `GColor fColor = {0, 0, 0, 1};`
   150→
   151→**STL Usage:**
   152→- `std::vector<>` for dynamic arrays: `std::vector<GColor> gradient_colors {};`
   153→- Vector initialization with empty braces: `{}`
   154→
   155→## JavaScript Conventions
   156→
   157→**DOM Manipulation:**
   158→- Event listeners attached via `addEventListener()`: `drawBtn.addEventListener('click', drawShape);`
   159→- Arrow functions used in callbacks: `opacitySlider.addEventListener('input', (e) => { ... })`
   160→- CSS class manipulation for state: `classList.add()`, `classList.remove()`
   161→- Inline style manipulation when immediate feedback needed: `animateBtn.style.background = '#e74c3c'`
   162→
   163→**Async Operations:**
   164→- `async/await` pattern for hashing: `async function sha256(message) { ... }`
   165→- Web Crypto API usage: `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', msgBuffer)`
   166→- `sessionStorage` for client-side session state
   167→
   168→**HTML Canvas:**
   169→- Canvas context obtained via `getContext('2d')`
   170→- State management via `ctx.save()` and `ctx.restore()`
   171→- Canvas drawing operations use familiar patterns: `fillRect()`, `beginPath()`, `fill()`, `stroke()`
   172→
   173→---
   174→
   175→*Convention analysis: 2026-02-02*
   176→

1→/**
     2→ * Basic Instructions Walkthrough Program
     3→ *
     4→ * Demonstrates all 8 core RISC instruction types through a simple program that:
     5→ * - Loads immediate values into registers
     6→ * - Performs register arithmetic
     7→ * - Executes memory load/store operations
     8→ * - Takes a branch
     9→ * - Performs a jump
    10→ *
    11→ * This program is designed for educational purposes to show how each instruction
    12→ * type behaves in the 5-stage pipeline.
    13→ *
    14→ * Requires: InstructionSet
    15→ */
    16→(function() {
    17→  'use strict';
    18→
    19→  /**
    20→   * Basic Instructions Program
    21→   *
    22→   * Expected final state:
    23→   * - $8 = 10
    24→   * - $9 = 20
    25→   * - $10 = 30 (ADD result)
    26→   * - $11 = 10 (SUB result)
    27→   * - $12 = 30 (LW result)
    28→   * - mem[10] = 30 (SW result)
    29→   */
    30→  const BASIC_PROGRAM = {
    31→    name: "Basic Instructions Walkthrough",
    32→    description: "Demonstrates all 8 core RISC instruction types: register arithmetic, immediates, memory load/store, branch, and jump.",
    33→    instructions: [
    34→      // Step 1: Load immediate values into registers
    35→      Object.assign(
    36→        InstructionSet.createInstruction('ADDI', { rs: 0, rt: 8, immediate: 10 }),
    37→        { comment: 'Load 10 into $8: $8 = $0 + 10' }
    38→      ),
    39→      Object.assign(
    40→        InstructionSet.createInstruction('ADDI', { rs: 0, rt: 9, immediate: 20 }),
    41→        { comment: 'Load 20 into $9: $9 = $0 + 20' }
    42→      ),
    43→
    44→      // Step 2: Register arithmetic
    45→      Object.assign(
    46→        InstructionSet.createInstruction('ADD', { rs: 8, rt: 9, rd: 10 }),
    47→        { comment: 'Add registers: $10 = $8 + $9 = 30' }
    48→      ),
    49→      Object.assign(
    50→        InstructionSet.createInstruction('SUB', { rs: 9, rt: 8, rd: 11 }),
    51→        { comment: 'Subtract registers: $11 = $9 - $8 = 10' }
    52→      ),
    53→
    54→      // Step 3: Memory operations
    55→      Object.assign(
    56→        InstructionSet.createInstruction('SW', { rs: 8, rt: 10, immediate: 0 }),
    57→        { comment: 'Store $10 to memory: mem[$8 + 0] = mem[10] = 30' }
    58→      ),
    59→      Object.assign(
    60→        InstructionSet.createInstruction('LW', { rs: 8, rt: 12, immediate: 0 }),
    61→        { comment: 'Load from memory: $12 = mem[$8 + 0] = mem[10] = 30' }
    62→      ),
    63→

  </files>
  <action>
Create two new visualization components following the existing RegisterView/BlockDiagramView patterns (IIFE wrapper, window export, render(state) method).

**MemoryView (memory-view.js):**
- Class MemoryView with constructor(container) that creates a table layout inside the container
- render(state) method that:
  - Reads state.memory (Uint32Array, 256 words) and state.changedMemory (Set)
  - Filters to show only non-zero memory addresses (do NOT render all 256 rows)
  - Shows empty state message "No memory addresses in use" when all zeros
  - For each non-zero address: display byte address (wordIndex * 4) in hex (0x00000028 format), value in hex (0x0000001E format), and decimal value
  - Adds CSS class 'changed' to rows where state.changedMemory.has(wordIndex)
- Table structure: `<table class="memory-table">` with thead (Address | Hex Value | Decimal) and tbody
- Use helper function formatHex32(value) for consistent hex formatting: `'0x' + (value >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0').toUpperCase()`
- Container gets class 'memory-view', includes h3 "Data Memory" heading
- Export as window.MemoryView via IIFE pattern

**InstructionView (instruction-view.js):**
- Class InstructionView with constructor(container) that creates layout inside container
- render(state) method that:
  - Determines current instruction from state.pipeline.IF.instruction (Phase 10 decision: always read from IF.instruction regardless of active stage in non-pipelined mode)
  - Determines active stage by checking which stage has active=true (WB > MEM > EX > ID > IF priority)
  - If no instruction active: show "No instruction active" placeholder
  - If instruction active: show mnemonic with stage label (e.g., "ADD (EX stage)")
  - Show instruction fields based on InstructionSet.get(mnemonic).fields:
    - Opcode (always): the mnemonic string
    - rs (if definition.fields.rs): "$N" format
    - rt (if definition.fields.rt): "$N" format
    - rd (if definition.fields.rd): "$N" format
    - immediate (if definition.fields.immediate): decimal and hex
  - Show instruction comment if present (instruction.comment)
- Container gets class 'instruction-view', includes h3 "Current Instruction" heading
- Use CSS classes: .instruction-display, .instruction-mnemonic, .instruction-fields, .field, .field-name, .field-value, .instruction-comment
- Export as window.InstructionView via IIFE pattern

**Important:** Do NOT use innerHTML for the render() hot path on full table rewrites when a simple DOM update would suffice. However, since memory rows change dynamically (different addresses become non-zero), innerHTML on the tbody is acceptable and matches the RegisterView pattern.
  </action>
  <verify>
Verify files exist and follow patterns:
- `[ -f cpu-simulator/src/visualization/memory-view.js ] && echo "FOUND"`

- grep for "render(state)" in both files

- grep for "pipeline.IF.instruction" in instruction-view.js
  </verify>
  <done>
MemoryView renders non-zero memory addresses in hex table with changed-address highlighting.
InstructionView shows current instruction mnemonic, active stage, decoded fields (rs/rt/rd/immediate), and comment.
Both components follow IIFE + window export pattern and accept render(state) calls.
  </done>
</task>

<task type="auto">
  <name>Task 2: Create InstructionList component and update CSS</name>
  <files>
    cpu-simulator/src/ui/instruction-list.js
    cpu-simulator/src/visualization/visualization.css
  </files>
  <action>
Create the InstructionList component and add CSS styles for all three new components.

**InstructionList (instruction-list.js):**
- Class InstructionList with constructor(container, engine) where engine is an AnimationEngine instance
- loadProgram(program, frameSequence) method that:
  - Stores program.instructions reference
  - Builds instruction-to-frame map by scanning frameSequence.frames: for each frame where frame.pipeline.IF.active is true, record the first frame index for each unique PC value (pc / 4 = instruction index). Use Map: instructionIndex -> frameIndex. Only record first IF frame per instruction index.
  - Renders an ordered list (`<ol class="instruction-list">`) of program instructions
  - Each `<li class="instruction-item">` shows: mnemonic, operands ($rd, $rs, $rt, immediate as applicable), and comment if present
  - Items with valid frame mappings get tabindex="0" for keyboard accessibility
  - Wire click handlers: on click, call this.engine.jumpToFrame(frameIndex) with the mapped frame index
  - Wire keyboard handlers: Enter or Space on focused item also calls jumpToFrame
- Private method _updateCurrentInstruction() called on 'cpu:framechange' event:
  - Reads engine.getCurrentState() to find which instruction is currently in IF stage
  - Adds 'active' class to the corresponding list item, removes from all others
  - Auto-scrolls active item into view with scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'nearest' }) - but ONLY when engine is NOT playing (check engine.isPlaying to avoid scroll jank during playback)
- Private method _formatOperands(instruction) that formats register and immediate fields
- Container gets class 'instruction-list-container', includes h3 "Program Instructions"
- Listen to window 'cpu:framechange' event in constructor to call _updateCurrentInstruction
- Export as window.InstructionList via IIFE pattern

**CSS Updates (visualization.css):**
Append new sections to the existing visualization.css file for all three new components:

Memory View styles:
- `.memory-view` container with appropriate padding
- `.memory-view h3` heading style
- `.memory-table-container` with max-height: 300px, overflow-y: auto for scrollable table
- `.memory-table` as full-width table with border-collapse
- `.memory-table thead th` with sticky positioning, background, bold, border-bottom
- `.memory-row` with transition: background-color 300ms ease-out
- `.memory-row.changed` with background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow)
- `.memory-address`, `.memory-value` in monospace font (var(--font-mono))
- `.empty-state` centered, muted text

Instruction View styles:
- `.instruction-view` container
- `.instruction-display` card-like container
- `.instruction-mnemonic .value` in bold, monospace
- `.instruction-fields` as flex-wrap layout
- `.field` with inline display, padding, background: var(--color-surface-alt), border-radius
- `.field-name` bold, `.field-value` monospace
- `.instruction-comment` italicized, muted color

Instruction List styles:
- `.instruction-list-container` with max-height: 400px, overflow-y: auto
- `.instruction-list` as ordered list (list-style-position: inside)
- `.instruction-item` with padding, border-bottom, cursor: pointer, transition
- `.instruction-item:hover` subtle background highlight
- `.instruction-item.active` with left border highlight using var(--stage-if-color) and light background
- `.instruction-item:focus-visible` with outline for keyboard accessibility
- `.inst-mnemonic` bold, monospace
- `.inst-operands` monospace
- `.inst-comment` italicized, muted

All new styles should respect `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` by disabling transitions.
  </action>

  <done>

<task type="checkpoint:human-verify" gate="blocking">
  <name>Task 2: Verify interactive demo page</name>
  <what-built>
Complete interactive CPU simulator demo page with all visualization components, playback controls, program switching, and keyboard navigation.
  </what-built>
  <how-to-verify>
1. Open cpu-simulator/index.html in Chrome/Firefox
2. Verify initial state: Block diagram visible, registers showing, "Basic Instructions Walkthrough" selected
3. Click "Step Fwd" button - verify:
   - Block diagram highlights IF stage components
   - Register grid updates (may not change on first step)
   - Instruction list highlights first instruction
   - Current instruction view shows instruction details
   - Frame counter updates (e.g., "Frame 1 of 45")
4. Click "Step Fwd" several more times - verify memory view shows values after SW instruction executes
5. Click "Step Back" - verify frame goes backward
6. Click "Play" - verify auto-advancing; click "Pause" to stop
7. Change speed to "4x" - click "Play" - verify faster playback
